title: A thin onion margin that breaks under stress
summary: Lasalgaon → Vashi New Mumbai, January 2021: a ₹490 per quintal median price gap on 20 matched days. After modeled costs: ₹136 per quintal on the typical day.
why_selected: Chosen automatically for January 2021: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 20 matched report days.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices; sale matched to the first destination report 1–3 days after transit
caveats: Hypothetical: no actual shipment is claimed.
Modal prices may mix varieties and grades (mostly FAQ).
Costs are survey values and assumptions, not quotes.
OSRM car profile; truck route not verified.

scenes.headline: January 2021
scenes.caption: The short road from Nashik's onion belt to Mumbai's wholesale market at Vashi.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 20 matched days, Lasalgaon reported a median ₹2,560 per quintal; Vashi New Mumbai reported ₹2,950 1 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹490/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹490 per quintal and was positive on 95% of days.

scenes.headline: 217 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 217 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~3 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 1 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹47/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: ₹136 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes −₹29 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 13 of 20 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would have shipped on 15 of 20 days, averaging ₹231 per quintal; 2 of those shipments lost money.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: A modeled surplus survived baseline costs but not the stress test, so it depended on everything going right. A trader acting on the previous report did average ₹231 per quintal under baseline costs and ₹69 under stress: thin, modeled, and not proof of a real trade.

assumptions.value: scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹47/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days

conclusion: A modeled surplus survived baseline costs but not the stress test, so it depended on everything going right. A trader acting on the previous report did average ₹231 per quintal under baseline costs and ₹69 under stress: thin, modeled, and not proof of a real trade.

title: The month onion prices jumped across India
summary: In June 2021, the median onion market moved +25.0% in a month, 2.5 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 2.5σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for onion, across 559 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: June 2021
scenes.caption: Onion prices across 559 markets that reported in both May 2021 and June 2021.

scenes.headline: Median move +25.0%
scenes.caption: The typical market's onion price jumped 25.0% in one month. 87% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 2.5× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 2.5 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Maharashtra
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 49 reporting markets in Maharashtra had a median change of +48.7%.

scenes.headline: Gurgaon
scenes.caption: Gurgaon (Haryana), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹1,150 → ₹1,700 per quintal (+47.8%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.
